nodes.label: LiteLLM Lacks Effective-Dated History
nodes.rationale: LiteLLM overwrites price fields in place with no effective_date/start_date/end_date field, so it cannot answer 'what did this model cost at timestamp T' without external history reconstruction.

nodes.label: Codex Fork/Subagent Lineage Reconstruction
nodes.rationale: Fork/subagent rollouts can begin with a re-stamped copy of the parent transcript; Agentsview compares the ordered turn_context.turn_id sequence as opaque identifiers against the parent and discards leading turns already present in the parent to isolate child-owned usage.

nodes.label: Codex Incremental Checkpoints and Streamed Full Imports Design
nodes.norm_label: codex incremental checkpoints and streamed full imports design

nodes.label: Codex Append Cursor Contract
nodes.rationale: LRU cursor cache keyed by path/offset/inode holds compact continuation state only, bounded to 256 entries and 2 MiB, so warm parsing scales with appended records not transcript history.

nodes.label: Cross-Sync Tool Results as Transactional Deltas
nodes.norm_label: cross-sync tool results as transactional deltas
nodes.rationale: A tool output appended after its call was persisted no longer forces a full re-parse; deferred result updates are applied with targeted probes instead.

nodes.label: Persistent Safe-Resume Checkpoints
nodes.rationale: A full parse captures a resumable SHA-256 state, trailing 128 KiB anchor digest, and file identity in one pass so unchanged files skip transcript reads and eligible appends resume from a stored offset.

nodes.label: Prepared-lowercase-text caching for find matching
nodes.rationale: Each stable content block weakly owns prepared lowercase text and queries compile once per scan so repeated queries don't refold every character; only length-changing folds need packed expansion boundaries, keeping matching cheap without capping or omitting results.

nodes.label: Extraction Generation Fingerprint
nodes.rationale: SHA-256 over protocol version, model identity+deployment (endpoint excluded so moving a deployment doesn't orphan the corpus), segmenter name/params, prompt digests, and request shape; any change builds a new generation instead of mixing outputs.

nodes.label: Model Client Recovery Ladder
nodes.rationale: Transient failures retry with backoff; permanent rejections fail fast; overflow/truncation recursively halve unit text down to a floor bounded by a fixed max call count so one oversized message cannot fan out unbounded model calls.

nodes.label: TurnsV1 Segmentation
nodes.rationale: Derives intent/action units at turn granularity with deterministic ordering so resume cursors and entry identity survive restarts/upgrades; splits at ordinal discontinuities because evidence provenance requires gap-free ranges.

nodes.label: Recall Privacy Eligibility Boundary
nodes.rationale: Eligibility enforced in SQL and re-checked in Go, fails closed on missing/stale scan versions, and requires zero secret findings of any confidence (not just definite leaks) because candidate findings are exactly what must not reach the model.

nodes.label: Recall Measurement and Data Lifecycle Ledger
nodes.norm_label: recall measurement and data lifecycle ledger

nodes.label: pg serve Raw-Sync Route Registration
nodes.rationale: Raw-sync routes are gated on the PostgreSQL role having write access to every raw-sync table plus the ingest-job sequence, so a read-only role safely continues serving the normal UI without those routes.

nodes.label: Hosted Raw Sync Security Boundary
nodes.rationale: Hosted raw sync is not end-to-end encrypted because the server must read retained source files to parse them; production deployments must add TLS, encryption at rest, and access controls separately.

nodes.label: AgentsView Privacy Model
nodes.rationale: Session data stays on the local machine by default; the server binds to 127.0.0.1 unless remote access is explicitly configured, and data leaves only for opt-in features.

nodes.label: Push Order as Consistency Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Because ClickHouse lacks multi-statement transactions, dependent rows are inserted before stale rows are deleted and before session rows are inserted, so a crash at any step leaves state that a retry can repair rather than losing data.

nodes.label: ClickHouse Mirror Rejected Alternatives
nodes.rationale: Pasting PostgreSQL/DuckDB SQL fails on ClickHouse 25.8 semantics; plain MergeTree with delete-then-insert risks a crash window with no content; CollapsingMergeTree needs old rows for cancel rows; a generic remote-mirror package would not fit ClickHouse's distinct DSN/TLS/SQL shape.

nodes.label: ReplacingMergeTree(push_version) Table Design
nodes.rationale: push_version as Unix-nanosecond push start time lets same-key retried rows collapse on merge and read via final=1, avoiding CollapsingMergeTree's need for cancel rows.

nodes.label: Shared Filter Builder, ClickHouse Dialect
nodes.rationale: Keeps SQLite/PostgreSQL/DuckDB SQL byte-identical while ClickHouse gets its own dialect hooks (UNION ALL, IN (SELECT) instead of correlated EXISTS, toStartOfDay instead of date_trunc) to work around MergeTree SQL limitations.

nodes.label: ClickHouse Write Model (from DuckDB) + Operator Model (from PostgreSQL)
nodes.norm_label: clickhouse write model (from duckdb) + operator model (from postgresql)
nodes.rationale: Whole-session replace gated by a fingerprint on the session row with a cursor in the mirror, borrowing DuckDB's write model and PostgreSQL's operator model rather than either's exact mechanism, so a reset mirror repairs itself on next push.

nodes.label: MCP Daemon-Backed Reads Design
nodes.rationale: MCP does not open the local SQLite archive directly so MCP reads stay on the same daemon policy as the desktop app and avoid a long-running MCP process holding its own archive handle.

nodes.label: MCP Security Notes
nodes.rationale: MCP tools are read-only, but exposed prompts, responses, tool output, and usage totals are still sensitive, so stdio and loopback binds are preferred and non-loopback endpoints require bearer tokens.

nodes.label: One-Way Sync Limitation
nodes.rationale: Sync direction is SQLite to PostgreSQL only, so changes in PostgreSQL do not propagate back and permanent deletes are not propagated because local rows no longer exist at push time.

nodes.label: Matryoshka Dimension Reduction (request_dimensions)
nodes.rationale: request_dimensions asks Matryoshka-trained models to serve shorter vectors server-side, trading some recall for a smaller/faster index; never faked client-side because a mismatched endpoint response is rejected rather than truncated locally.

nodes.norm_label: hour and day export documents (schema v3)

nodes.label: Pydantic GenAI Prices v2 Pricing Catalog
nodes.norm_label: pydantic genai prices v2 pricing catalog

nodes.label: Pin Reconciliation by source_uuid
nodes.rationale: Pins are keyed by a stable source_uuid derived from the underlying message so a pin survives a re-parse that shifts message ordinals, instead of silently drifting to the wrong message.

nodes.label: Content Digest for Correction Screening
nodes.rationale: Each hour includes a SHA-256 content digest so integrations can detect corrections and replace saved hours without re-fetching everything; day digest is SHA-256 over the ordered 24 hour digests.

nodes.label: Session Usage Subagent Deduplication
nodes.rationale: Claude Code echoes parent turns into a subagent sidechain transcript, so cost/token totals are derived from one deduplicated row set to avoid double-counting the same message across parent and child sessions.

nodes.label: Session CLI Transport Selection Logic
nodes.rationale: CLI proxies to a running writable daemon over HTTP when available, opens read-only SQLite directly for cold-archive reads, and starts a detached daemon only when fresh data or writes are needed, keeping SQLite writes owned by a single process.

nodes.label: Copilot Reported Billing (totalNanoAiu)
nodes.rationale: When an authoritative Copilot totalNanoAiu billing total is present, AgentsView suppresses catalog-priced estimates for that session to prevent double counting across models, days, and resumed segments.

nodes.label: Pricing Source (LiteLLM + OpenRouter merge)
nodes.rationale: LiteLLM and OpenRouter catalogs are fetched and merged, with LiteLLM's rate winning on conflict and OpenRouter filling gaps, so uncommon models still get priced; embedded fallback keeps offline use functional.

nodes.label: Full Resync (non-destructive re-parse)
nodes.rationale: Full resync re-parses all session files from scratch using a non-destructive flow that preserves existing session data and carries forward orphaned sessions, useful after upgrades or misparses.

nodes.label: Claude Code Subagent Attribution Rules
nodes.rationale: Task-tool subagents are written to their own transcripts with isSidechain:true and the parent's sessionId; each is ingested as its own session linked via relationship_type=subagent and attributed to the parent only at presentation time, because subagent spend is real billed spend the parent transcript never records (45-77% cost undercount observed without this rollup).

nodes.label: Claude Code Web Search Billing Reconstruction
nodes.norm_label: claude code web search billing reconstruction
nodes.rationale: CLI WebSearch runs as an out-of-band side call never written to the transcript; Agentsview credits the assistant message with its linked tool result's searchCount instead of the zeroed usage.server_tool_use counter, falling back to the message's own counter when nonzero, to avoid double counting.

nodes.label: Pricing Precedence Rationale
nodes.rationale: Custom rate beats Pydantic conditional rate beats flat catalog; events without a valid timestamp skip Pydantic because choosing its oldest conditional record would invent a historical date.

nodes.label: Changelog Plain-Language Rule
nodes.rationale: Each changelog bullet must start with the user/operator-visible outcome, with implementation detail only when it changes what the reader should do, to keep 0.36.0-0.42.0 entries understandable without prior context.

nodes.label: DuckDB FTS/BM25 search deferred
nodes.rationale: The DuckDB FTS extension works locally but BM25 lookup does not resolve through Quack-attached catalogs, so indexed DuckDB search stays deferred until local and remote behavior line up, keeping substring/regex fallback for now.

nodes.label: DuckDB schema avoids TIMESTAMP DEFAULT current_timestamp
nodes.norm_label: duckdb schema avoids timestamp default current_timestamp
nodes.rationale: Current Quack attach rejects catalogs with dynamic-default TIMESTAMP columns, so writers must supply current_timestamp explicitly; a schema-version change builds and validates a fresh mirror before atomically swapping it in.

nodes.label: Local by default, shared when you choose
nodes.norm_label: local by default, shared when you choose
nodes.rationale: Agent transcripts are highly sensitive, so AgentsView starts with one local SQLite archive and a loopback-only server; data leaves the machine only when a specific sharing feature (PostgreSQL sync, remote DuckDB, Generated Insights, GitHub publishing, hosted raw sync) is explicitly enabled.

nodes.label: console/ subdir ID collision fix fixture
nodes.norm_label: console/ subdir id collision fix fixture

nodes.label: Whitespace-insensitive QwenPaw parser
nodes.rationale: Pretty-printed fixture output isn't byte-identical to a live runtime's compact JSON, but the parser is whitespace-insensitive so pretty-printed fixtures remain valid test input.

nodes.label: Tool-Result Image Offload
nodes.rationale: Keeps supported tool-result images in {dataDir}/assets instead of embedding bytes in SQLite to bound database size, while remaining recoverable from inline source bytes on write failure.

nodes.label: Streamed Cold Imports (staging sink)
nodes.rationale: A staging sink writes event rows into a scratch SQLite database while the in-memory model keeps only placeholders, trading CPU for lower transient memory on cold imports over 128 MiB.

nodes.label: Watcher Runtime Contract
nodes.rationale: 500ms batching window with serialized callbacks at least five seconds apart, and an 8192-path/2MiB batch cap that collapses to a full-sync marker when exceeded, bounds memory without losing changes.

nodes.label: Frontend tests (npm run check / test / e2e)
nodes.norm_label: frontend tests (npm run check / test / e2e)

nodes.label: CGO + SQLite FTS5 requirement
nodes.rationale: SQLite FTS5 requires CGO, so a C compiler is mandatory on every platform; skipping -tags fts5 or CGO produces a binary that fails at runtime on FTS queries rather than at compile time.

nodes.label: Durability Quality Standard
nodes.rationale: A capable engineer should understand what changed, why, and how behavior is protected using only lasting repository artifacts, without needing the original agent session or private context.

nodes.label: docs-assets / docs-generated-assets orphan branches
nodes.rationale: Images are kept on separate asset branches so normal clones do not download screenshots and large media.

nodes.label: Screenshot Capture Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Filters and redacts a disposable SQLite snapshot before it ever reaches Docker/Playwright, and excludes private terms and original machine names, so generated marketing/docs screenshots cannot leak real user data.

nodes.label: Outcome-First Changelog Rule
nodes.rationale: Leads with user-visible outcomes before implementation detail, and requires 'local-first system of record' in the subline rather than an absolute 'no cloud services' claim, since hosted raw sync now makes local-by-default the accurate privacy boundary.

nodes.label: GPT-5.6 Sol (model)
nodes.rationale: Pricing dropped 2026-08-21 as promotional pricing; old rates preserved historically via Pydantic PR #592 rather than overwritten, so pre-cutoff usage can still be priced correctly.

nodes.label: Layered Pricing Source Recommendation
nodes.rationale: Keep LiteLLM as required current catalog for breadth/speed; use Pydantic GenAI Prices as optional first-pass historical/conditional layer falling through to LiteLLM; treat Portkey as licensed cross-check; exclude tokencost (stale copy) and Helicone (missing probe models) as fallbacks.

nodes.label: benchgate (cmd/benchgate)
nodes.rationale: Builds on golang.org/x/perf benchfmt/benchmath; adds thresholds/floors/failing exit code. Gates allocs/op hard (1.25x, worst-vs-median, deterministic), B/op with 1.35x median+significance, sec/op with 2.0x median+significance, to tolerate CI noise while catching O(archive)-not-O(delta) regressions.

nodes.norm_label: real daemon synthetic sqlite producer capture

nodes.label: Performance Regression History
nodes.rationale: agentsview repeatedly shipped regressions where sync work scaled with archive size instead of new data (discovery O(sources), reparsed unchanged sources, O(history) incremental appends, warm Codex appends, bulk ingest, event storms, per-row query shape, usage archive scaling); each class now has a deterministic work-count invariant test.

nodes.label: OpenCode Virtual-Event WAL Sidecar Fix
nodes.rationale: Preparation now removes successfully resolved OpenCode virtual members from the missing-path list because changed-path prep had treated virtual paths as missing filesystem entries even after resolution, triggering expensive container-wide existence checks (20.7x speedup measured).

nodes.label: Dedup Exception Tier
nodes.rationale: A dedup group is only finalized into daily rows when its resolution provably cannot vary with query window or live filters (single session/date/model/headless state, no snapshot-general link, no order-dependent Copilot cost, unique identity); irreducible groups stay as narrow exceptions so exception volume scales with genuine cross-session duplicates, not token volume.

nodes.label: Aggregate Cache Freshness Contract
nodes.rationale: sync_marker is not monotonic (can decrease), so installation compares complete source fingerprints after extraction rather than ordering by marker value; races retry at most three times then fail rather than return stale usage.

nodes.label: Stats Outcome Rollup (4 outcomes -> 3 buckets)
nodes.rationale: The raw four outcomes (completed/abandoned/errored/unknown) are rolled up into success/failure/unknown for both human summary and JSON to simplify the aggregate reporting surface.

nodes.label: Recall Evidence and Trust Model
nodes.rationale: Each entry's evidence records exact message ordinals and a content digest; if an anchored message disappears or changes, provenance is revoked and sticky, so later parser output cannot silently restore trust.

nodes.label: Generation Fingerprint Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Fingerprint covers model, dimension, chunking, and prefix/suffix params so any input change cuts a new generation, guaranteeing vectors in one generation are always produced by one reproducible embedding configuration.

nodes.label: vectors.db Storage Layout
nodes.rationale: A separate SQLite database (not tables inside the archive) survives a parser-change resync/swap untouched and never needs the archive open to serve a query; tables inside the archive were rejected because they would tie vector writes to the archive's write path/lock and complicate the resync-swap story.

nodes.label: Unit Documents (user messages + assistant runs)
nodes.rationale: Embedding whole assistant runs instead of individual short procedural messages collapses ~1.1 million assistant messages into ~44k documents, cutting embedding cost roughly 25x while capturing whole narrative arcs.

nodes.label: PR Dispatcher Workflow Pattern
nodes.rationale: The PR dispatcher always calls the main-pinned reusable workflow so that Linux AMD64 and Windows jobs run on Namespace runners for every pull request, including fork PRs, since forks cannot be trusted with persistent self-hosted runner access.

nodes.label: Self-Hosted Runner Path Pinning Policy
nodes.rationale: Persistent self-hosted macOS runners must never be selectable from a workflow definition controlled by a pull request; the organization's runner-group policy pins access to the exact workflow file path on refs/heads/main only, so these workflows are push-only on main.

nodes.rationale: huma.DefaultArrayNullable is set false so encoding/json/v2's nil-slice-as-empty-array behavior matches a consistent non-nullable array contract in OpenAPI 3.1 and on the wire.

nodes.label: Route Group File Ownership Rule
nodes.rationale: Route registration and handlers live in the file that owns the path so OpenAPI ownership stays close to runtime behavior; shared plumbing is factored out only when at least two route groups need it.

nodes.label: disabled_agents Config Boundary
nodes.community_name: Scoped Push and Provider Controls Design
nodes.rationale: Disabling a provider changes only local filesystem ingestion; remote import, all export paths, and RemoteSyncExcluded stay independent so disabling never deletes or hides archived sessions and cannot be confused with the permanent export-safety boundary.

nodes.label: Gemini Zero-Session Fast Path
nodes.community_name: Scoped Push and Provider Controls Design
nodes.rationale: Defers building the Gemini project metadata map until a session file is actually found, avoiding hashing projects.json or resolving missing Git roots for roots that exist only for unrelated tools.

nodes.label: Preserve Watcher Batches End to End (Chosen Approach)
nodes.community_name: Scoped Push and Provider Controls Design
nodes.norm_label: preserve watcher batches end to end (chosen approach)
nodes.rationale: Selected over 'assume the daemon watcher already synchronized the change' because the two watchers and the HTTP request are independent and a race could publish stale archive state; selected over provider-disabling alone because that would still let every watch push rediscover all remaining providers.

nodes.label: HTTP Remote Sync Incremental Mirror
nodes.rationale: Curated per-provider exports (Cursor transcripts only, VS Code Copilot chat sessions only, Windsurf sanitized snapshot) exist so caches, extension state, and credentials near session files never enter the manifest, archive, or mirror.

nodes.label: Hand-Authored Go Test Expectations Rationale
nodes.rationale: Go-side test expectations are kept hand-authored rather than generated so the fixture producer is not also the test oracle, preserving an independent check on the parser.

nodes.label: DuckDB One-Way Mirror Design
nodes.rationale: Data flows from SQLite to DuckDB only; DuckDB/Quack are read-only backends that never ingest session files directly, keeping SQLite as the sole source of truth.

nodes.label: agentsview.one-shot-usage Result Contract
nodes.rationale: Closed schema/version and closed enum values so consumers must reject unknown values; a present zero token field is proven zero while an omitted field is unavailable, and money uses exact integer-microdollar objects, never floats.

nodes.label: Tray Setup Failure Ordering
nodes.rationale: Window-lifecycle (close interception) setup only runs after tray creation succeeds, so a tray setup failure preserves normal close behavior instead of hiding the window with no tray surface to restore it from.
